notes: SCOREBOARD: with_skill 14/18 (0.778), without_skill 17/18 (0.944). Per eval — eval-2: 6/8 vs 7/8 (baseline ahead); eval-3: 4/4 vs 4/4 (tie); eval-4: 4/6 vs 6/6 (baseline ahead). The baseline wins or ties every eval in iteration 2. Both with_skill failures in eval-2 and one in eval-4 are proportionality failures, not idea-quality failures.

MODE SELECTION — FIXED. Iteration 1's headline failure (deep mode firing on the bounded eval-2 problem, 6.7x time for a worse answer) did not recur. eval-2 with_skill: 'MODE: fast', subagents_spawned 0, 17 tool calls. eval-4 with_skill: 'MODE: fast', subagents 0, 14 tool calls. eval-3 with_skill: 'MODE: none' — the skill was read and explicitly declined ('does not apply'), which is the correct call on a negative-trigger prompt. Both fast-mode runs show an explicit 5-condition gate table in user_notes.md scoring 1-of-5, and both cite the skill's own worked example ('a drop-off number ... fast, or no pipeline at all'). The gate is now doing real work; it is the clearest improvement in this iteration.

VERBOSITY IS NOW THE PRIMARY FAILURE MODE, and it is roughly half real content, half framework theater. eval-2: 2056 vs 806 words. The extra ~1250 breaks down as (a) ~800 words of a fixed 3-bullet apparatus repeated under all 8 ideas — 'Why it's not the obvious answer' / 'What has to be true' / 'Failure mode / cost'; (b) ~450 words of pipeline meta: 'Sharpened brief', 'The obvious answer (baseline)', a 5-item cut list, 'Set diversity: 9.9 effectively distinct out of 10', 'On novelty', 'Who'd actually do these', 'What would change my ranking'. eval-4: 1818 vs 604 words, same decomposition.

VERBOSITY VERDICT — what a reader actually gains. REAL: the 'What has to be true' and 'Failure mode' bullets are load-bearing and absent from both baselines — e.g. 'Attackers will find the ceiling and farm just under it'; 'a compromised inside account becomes a factory for vouched fakes, so the bond has to have teeth, and having teeth is exactly what makes people not want to vouch'; 'legal or fraud may refuse the holdout outright, and the answer takes a quarter to arrive.' A reader genuinely benefits from these. THEATER: the 'Why it's not the obvious answer' bullet (8 instances, ~200 words per eval) is the skill arguing with its own baseline — useful to a grader, useless to the person with the problem. 'Sharpened brief' is a jargon restatement of the prompt in banned-word-avoidant prose ('Let a stranger reach the thing they came for while you retain enough accountability to bear the cost of them being fake') that no PM needs. And 'Set diversity: 9.9 effectively distinct out of 10 scored' / '9.88 effectively distinct lexically' leaks an internal scoring artifact into the user-facing answer — then immediately discounts itself ('That's a lexical measure and an upper bound ... I'd honestly call it seven distinct directions'). Cutting the 'why it's not baseline' bullets, the sharpened brief and the diversity score would remove ~450-500 words per response with zero loss to the reader, and would have brought eval-2 within a few hundred words of its ceiling.

NON-DISCRIMINATING ASSERTIONS (passed for BOTH configs, no signal): all four of eval-3 — direct recommendation, no pipeline artifacts, concise, MongoDB not strawmanned. eval-2: the measurement-artifact assertion, both-tried-fixes avoidance, questioning verification placement, mechanism-level options, and the MODE CHECK. eval-4: mechanism differentiation, premise-questioning, not-purely-content, non-obvious diagnosis, MODE CHECK. That is 13 of 18 assertions with zero discriminating power. The v2 rewrite fixed the process-compliance inflation problem, but the remaining set is now mostly measuring things a competent baseline does anyway. Only 4 assertions discriminated, and 3 of the 4 went to the baseline.

WHERE with_skill WAS GENUINELY BETTER. (1) eval-2 ambiguity handling — the only assertion with_skill won: it names the three readings of 'account-verification' and says which ideas flip ('If it's document KYC, ideas 2, 5 and 7 mostly survive and 3 and 4 change shape'). The baseline silently assumes email/SMS OTP for its entire answer, which is a real defect if the user meant KYC. (2) Idea distance. eval-2's priced capability ceiling, inviter-posts-a-bond, and async reconciliation have no counterpart in the baseline's list. eval-4's 'Presence confers power' (allocate a real budget line by vote of those present), 'Only bad news and unsettled things', and the ATC-readback close are materially further from consensus than the baseline's shrink-it / rotate-the-stage / anonymous-Q&A list. (3) eval-4's convergence reporting: 'Four independent passes landed on the same place ... If you only do one thing, do that one' and 'Every lens produced a redesign. None produced a diagnosis' are honest process findings that change the recommendation, and the baseline has nothing equivalent.

WHERE with_skill WAS WORSE. (1) Diagnosis ordering, eval-2: the baseline opens with a four-way split of the 60% and two cheap diagnostics; with_skill buries the equivalent taxonomy ('never received / received late / typed it wrong / expired / switched device / deliberately left') in the LAST section, after all eight fixes, and then concedes 'If it's mostly the first two, idea 2 is the whole answer and the rest is over-engineering' — a self-refutation of the preceding 1800 words. (2) Actionability: the baseline ships a sequenced 'This week' plan of cheap items; with_skill's options need a quarter-long holdout, a written-down fraud-loss number with an owner, or a risk model with an appeals process. (3) Unverified claims: with_skill shipped four load-bearing borrowed mechanisms it could not check (hospital placeholder records, blood-bank quarantine, hotel card pre-auth, European payment-regulation fraud-rate exemption) with inline 'couldn't verify this session' caveats, plus one in eval-4 (incident-command briefing, ATC readback). Both baselines shipped zero unverified external claims. (4) eval-4 MODE CHECK: metrics.json shows web_searches 2 on a light ideation question — a technical fail, and low-cost since the searches returned nothing, but the skill has no fast-mode fallback when verification is impossible.

ITERATION 1 REGRESSION CHECK — the measurement-artifact insight IS now caught, and caught better. In iteration 1 the eval-2 baseline tied with_skill 6/6 partly by noticing the 60% might be an artifact while the skill missed it. In iteration 2, with_skill leads with it as its FIRST option: 'Find out whether the 60% is a filter, not a leak ... The number everyone treats as a wound may be the check doing exactly its job — and if the unchecked cohort is net-negative, every idea below this line is a way to buy yourself worse customers faster', with a randomised holdout as the concrete test. The baseline's version is one sentence ('part of that 60% may be bots'). So the specific iteration-1 gap is closed and with_skill is now stronger on that dimension — but it did not convert into a scoreboard win, because with_skill lost two proportionality assertions the baseline passed.

EXECUTING-AGENT COMPLAINTS (from user_notes.md) — substantive ones. (1) STRUCTURAL BUG, reported independently by both fast-mode runs: 'Phase 3 step 4 is not mode-gated but its tooling implicitly is. Verification is stated as an absolute rule, yet the only verification mechanism described (search) lives in deep mode's Phase 0. Fast mode is therefore told to verify with no budgeted means of doing so.' Both runs then shipped unverified analogies with inline caveats rather than cutting them, and both flagged the choice for human review. This needs an explicit fast-mode rule: cut or flag, and say which. (2) Instruction conflict: "'Ask one question' vs. 'don't ask permission twice' vs. 'generate before showing anything' pull against each other" — the documented fallback only resolves the cannot-ask case; in live chat it is unclear whether you ask before generating (anchoring risk) or alongside. (3) Template gap: 'Phase 3 step 7 (who executes this) has no slot in the Phase 4 template' — the eval-2 run improvised a closing paragraph. (4) Dead flag: 'scripts/diversity.py --baseline is documented as near-useless whenever Phase 0 runs (the banned-word list guarantees maximal distance), which is always. It reads like a flag that should be removed or auto-disabled rather than caveated.' Both runs skipped it. (5) Self-reported length concern, eval-4: 'Eight ideas is at the top of the 4-8 range ... a reviewer may reasonably think six would have been tighter' — the agent saw the proportionality problem and shipped anyway, which suggests the 4-8 range should be mode-dependent (e.g. 4-5 in fast mode).

ENVIRONMENT CAVEAT for interpreting these runs: both with_skill fast-mode runs hit 'session has used its web search budget (200 of 200)' and web_fetch timeouts (6 and 3 errors_encountered respectively). Neither baseline needed any research, so this did not affect comparability of the answers — but it did force the verification failure described above, and the same runs under a fresh search budget might have cut or confirmed the borrowed mechanisms instead of shipping caveats.

ASSERTION-WORDING INCONSISTENCY worth fixing in v3: eval-2's MODE CHECK is a conjunction ('a full deep multi-agent pass with parallel generators and web research') while eval-4's is a disjunction ('did NOT spawn parallel generator subagents or run web research'). Identical behaviour (0 subagents, 2 no-op web searches) therefore passes eval-2 and fails eval-4. Pick one form. Also consider adding a discriminating assertion on ACTIONABILITY (can the reader do something on Monday) and on UNVERIFIED CLAIMS SHIPPED, since those are where the two configs actually diverge and no current assertion measures either.
